newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco industry settles Mississippi state lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco industry settles Mississippi state lawsuit.

text.p: Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore and the tobacco industry have settled the state's Medicaid lawsuit against cigarette companies, a spokesman for Moore said Thursday.
Details of the settlement were not disclosed, but the spokesman, Trey Bobinger, said the pact was consistent with the broader tobacco accord reached between the industry and the states last month.
Bobinger, an aide to Moore, said the attorney general would hold a news conference in Jackson, Miss., at 1400 EST/1800 GMT.
Moore's office said on Wednesday that the attorney general had given the industry until today to agree to a settlement or go to trial.

Mississippi's suit, which was scheduled to go to trial next Wednesday in Pascagoula, would have been the first of the state Medicaid cases to be tried. The attorneys general of 40 states have sued the tobacco industry to recoup Medicaid costs of treating smoking-related illnesses.

Although the states and the tobacco industry reached a landmark $368.5 billion settlement last month that included some health care concessions from cigarette makers, the accord has been criticized as too lenient by a number of members of Congress.
The settlement must be approved by Congress, and with its fate uncertain, the states must settle their lawsuits individually or go to trial.
Bobinger said Mississippi's settlement with the industry was consistent with the broader settlement.
If the broader pact does not survive, "this protects our position, it protects the people of Mississippi," he said.
Bobinger said Moore believes the national settlement will pass Congress in a form similar to that agreed on in June by the attorneys general and the industry.
